title: Nap Resistance Training
description: Baby refuses nap. Practices aggressive crawling drills across the living room.

choices.text: Crawl toward anything spherical
choices.flavor: Ball. Must reach ball. Blocks, stuffed animals, and books ignored. Only ball matters.

choices.text: Pull up on furniture and cruise around
choices.flavor: The coffee table is now a highway. Nothing in this house is safe.

title: High Chair Physics Lab
description: You throw food off the high chair repeatedly and study the bounce with scientific focus.

choices.text: Throw harder. Need more data.
choices.flavor: Peas travel six feet. Mashed potatoes stick to the wall. Research continues.

choices.text: Laugh after each throw and do it again
choices.flavor: The joy is in the repetition. Also in making Mom's eye twitch.

title: Gravity Test
description: You fall down. Again. But you laugh and immediately try to stand back up.

choices.text: Get right back up. No crying.
choices.flavor: Floor is temporary. Standing is the mission.

choices.text: Cry briefly, then get distracted and try again
choices.flavor: Two seconds of tears, then a butterfly. Then back to walking. Emotional range.

title: Territory Dispute
description: Older sibling has a toy. You want it. Negotiation is not in your vocabulary yet.

choices.text: Grab it and hold on with surprising grip strength
choices.flavor: Tiny hands, iron will. The toy is yours now. Possession is the law.

choices.text: Scream until an adult intervenes
choices.flavor: The scream works. It always works. Lungs are developing nicely.

title: Versus the Family Dog
description: You challenged the family dog to a race across the living room. Loss disputed. Rematch demanded.

choices.text: Demand a rematch immediately
choices.flavor: The dog won. You refuse to accept the results. The race was unfair. Four legs is cheating.

choices.text: Chase the dog around the yard instead
choices.flavor: The race becomes a pursuit. The dog thinks it is a game. You think it is training.

title: Throwing Contest
description: You turn everything into a throwing contest. Balls, toys, shoes, the remote.

choices.text: Throw as far as possible. Distance matters.
choices.flavor: The remote clears the couch. New personal record. Dad is not impressed.

choices.text: Aim for targets. Accuracy matters.
choices.flavor: The laundry basket is the goal. You hit it one out of ten times. Progress.

title: Made-Up Game Meltdown
description: You invented a game with your own rules. You still lost. This is unacceptable.

choices.text: Change the rules so you win retroactively
choices.flavor: Actually the floor is lava now and you were the only one not touching it. You win.

choices.text: Knock everything over and storm off
choices.flavor: Full tantrum. Blocks everywhere. But you come back in three minutes ready to play again.

title: The 'Mine' Phase
description: You say 'mine' to objects that are clearly not yours. The park bench. Another kid's snack. A bird.

choices.text: Claim everything. Expand the empire.
choices.flavor: The sandbox is yours. The slide is yours. Territorial instincts strong.

choices.text: Share when asked nicely
choices.flavor: You give back the shovel. Reluctantly. Growth is slow.

title: Backyard MVP
description: You declared yourself MVP of the backyard league. The league consists of you.

choices.text: Give yourself a trophy (a stick)
choices.flavor: The acceptance speech is mostly babbling but the confidence is real.

choices.text: Start training for next season immediately
choices.flavor: Run around the yard five times. Fall twice. Get up both times. Season prep complete.

title: The Fastest Player Ever
description: You pretend to be 'the fastest player ever.' You run the same route between the couch and the wall 20+ times.

choices.text: Run faster each time. Beat the record.
choices.flavor: The world record was 4 seconds. Now it is 3.8. The crowd goes wild. The crowd is the cat.

choices.text: Add commentary while running
choices.flavor: 'And he breaks through the defense!' Nobody is playing defense. The imagination is elite.

title: First Trash Talk
description: You tell your older sibling you are better at everything. Evidence is questionable.

choices.text: Double down. List every way you are better.
choices.flavor: 'I am faster, stronger, and I eat more chicken nuggets.' Devastating argument.

choices.text: Challenge them to prove it
choices.flavor: You lose the race badly but insist the starting position was unfair.

title: Repetition Machine
description: You found one physical activity you like and now you do it nonstop. Adults are baffled.

choices.text: Jump off the same step 40 times
choices.flavor: The landing technique improves by attempt 30. By attempt 40 it is automatic.

choices.text: Throw the same ball at the same wall forever
choices.flavor: Thud. Thud. Thud. The neighbors are concerned. You are focused.

title: Board Game Incident
description: You flipped the board after losing Candy Land. Investigation ongoing.

choices.text: Demand a rematch. Best of three.
choices.flavor: You lost two more. The board was flipped two more times. Pattern emerging.

choices.text: Apologize and reset the board
choices.flavor: Mom is proud. You still think the game was rigged, but you kept it together.

choices.text: Announce you are done with board games forever
choices.flavor: This boycott lasts approximately forty-five minutes.

title: Rules Lawyer
description: You learned the rules of tag. You immediately found a loophole.

choices.text: Exploit the loophole mercilessly
choices.flavor: 'Base' is wherever you are standing. Nobody agreed to this. You do not care.

choices.text: Suggest a rule change to make it fairer
choices.flavor: The other kids agree to your amendment. First legislative achievement.

title: Taking It Too Seriously
description: It is a casual game of kickball at recess. You are treating it like the Super Bowl.

choices.text: Play to win. Always.
choices.flavor: You kicked it over the fence. Home run. The game stopped because there is no ball now.

choices.text: Dial it back and let everyone have fun
choices.flavor: You still won, but people actually wanted to play with you again.

title: The Tall Climbing Wall
description: The big kids' climbing wall at the park. It is taller than you thought.

choices.text: Race to the top
choices.flavor: Hands scraped. Knees skinned. Made it to the top. Worth every scratch.

choices.text: Climb carefully, one handhold at a time
choices.flavor: Slow and steady. You made it. Less dramatic, equally effective.

choices.text: Watch from the ground
choices.flavor: Not today. You decide the swings are fine. Nothing wrong with knowing your limits.

title: Birthday Party Plan
description: It is your birthday. Your parents ask what kind of party you want.

choices.text: Sports party at the park
choices.flavor: Football, relay races, capture the flag. Your friends are exhausted but smiling.

choices.text: Big party with the whole class
choices.flavor: Everyone shows up. Cake, games, presents. You are the center of attention.

choices.text: Small party with close friends
choices.flavor: Just your best friends. Quality over quantity.

title: Wrestling in the Yard
description: Older cousin challenges you to wrestle in the grass. He is bigger but you are quick.

choices.text: Use speed and dodge around
choices.flavor: You are too fast to pin down. Your cousin cannot believe it.

choices.text: Try to power through
choices.flavor: You get tossed around but refuse to quit. Toughness matters.

title: Self-Imposed Benching
description: You benched yourself briefly after a bad play. Then immediately un-benched yourself.

choices.text: Storm back in with maximum intensity
choices.flavor: The benching lasted eleven seconds. The comeback was immediate and aggressive.

choices.text: Take a breath, then calmly rejoin
choices.flavor: Brief timeout. Emotional reset. Back in the game. Maturity: unlocked.

title: The Faster Kid
description: You notice another kid is faster than you. This is the first time this has happened.

choices.text: Challenge them to race every single day
choices.flavor: Monday: lost. Tuesday: lost. Wednesday: lost by less. Progress.

choices.text: Switch to something you are better at
choices.flavor: You cannot be the fastest at everything. But you can be the best at throwing.

choices.text: Convince yourself they got lucky
choices.flavor: The wind was helping them. Your shoes were untied. Many external factors.

title: The Bigger Kid
description: A bigger kid at school keeps pushing you around at lunch. Today they took your dessert.

choices.text: Stand up to them
choices.flavor: You puff up your chest and say NO. They are surprised. It does not go perfectly, but you earned respect.

choices.text: Tell a teacher
choices.flavor: The teacher handles it. The bully gets in trouble. System works.

choices.text: Walk away and avoid them
choices.flavor: You avoid the conflict. Smart, but it stings a little.

title: Homework vs. Outside
description: Mom says homework first. The sun is out. The neighborhood kids are already playing.

choices.text: Do the homework first, play after
choices.flavor: You knock it out in 20 minutes. Mom is impressed. You still caught the last hour of daylight.

choices.text: Play first, homework in the dark
choices.flavor: The homework is sloppy. The handwriting is illegible. But you scored three touchdowns.

choices.text: Negotiate a deal with Mom
choices.flavor: Half now, half later. Diplomacy wins. Both sides claim victory.

title: Talent Show Decision
description: The school talent show is coming up. Some kids are singing. Some are dancing.

choices.text: Do a sports trick routine on stage
choices.flavor: You juggle a ball on stage. The crowd goes wild. Future star energy.

choices.text: Help backstage instead
choices.flavor: You run the curtain and help other kids. The teacher calls you the MVP of the show.

choices.text: Skip it and play outside
choices.flavor: Not your thing. Free time better spent running.

title: Recess Conditioning
description: You ran laps during recess 'for conditioning.' Other kids are concerned.

choices.text: Keep running. This is the work.
choices.flavor: The teacher asked if you were being punished. You said no. She did not believe you.

choices.text: Recruit others to run with you
choices.flavor: Three kids join. Two quit after one lap. The third keeps up. Accountability partner found.

title: Self-Directed Practice
description: Nobody told you to practice. You went outside and threw a ball against the wall for an hour.

choices.text: Keep going until it gets dark
choices.flavor: Thud. Thud. Thud. The rhythm is meditative. Your arm is sore. You do not stop.

choices.text: Switch to a different drill after a while
choices.flavor: Throwing, then catching, then sprints. A full workout at age 6. Coaches would be impressed.

title: The Shortcut
description: During a race at field day, you notice you could cut a corner and nobody would see.

choices.text: Run the full course. Win it clean.
choices.flavor: You finish second. But you know the truth. And that matters more than a ribbon.

choices.text: Cut the corner. Nobody saw.
choices.flavor: You won. But something feels off. You cannot explain it yet.

title: First Structured Drills
description: An older kid at the park is showing everyone how to do proper football drills.

choices.text: Follow every instruction carefully
choices.flavor: You line up, set your feet, and run the route. The older kid says 'not bad.'

choices.text: Try to show off and go beyond the drill
choices.flavor: You add a spin move nobody asked for. It does not work. But the ambition is noted.

title: Report Card Day
description: Report cards are out. Yours is a mixed bag. Good at gym. Less good at sitting still.

choices.text: Promise to try harder in class
choices.flavor: You meant it. For about two weeks. Then recess happened.

choices.text: Shrug it off. You know what you are good at.
choices.flavor: Mom is not thrilled. But your PE grade is outstanding.

title: Neighborhood Draft
description: You organized a neighborhood draft for backyard football. No one else understood the rules.

choices.text: Pick the teams yourself. You are the commissioner.
choices.flavor: Draft order determined by rock-paper-scissors. Appeals process: none.

choices.text: Let everyone pick and just play
choices.flavor: Less drama, more football. The game starts in under five minutes for once.

title: Unofficial Scorekeeper
description: You are keeping score in a game where nobody asked for a scorekeeper.

choices.text: Announce the score loudly after every play
choices.flavor: 'That is 14-7!' Nobody cares. You care enough for everyone.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself and use it as motivation
choices.flavor: You know you are down by one touchdown. Nobody else does. Quiet competitiveness.

title: The Kid to Beat
description: There is one kid who is clearly better than everyone else. You have been studying how they play.

choices.text: Challenge them directly and compete head to head
choices.flavor: You lost. But you made them work for it. They noticed.

choices.text: Practice in secret and wait for the right moment
choices.flavor: Extra hours in the yard. When the moment comes, you will be ready.

title: Cannot Stop
description: Nobody told you to keep going. You just did not want to stop throwing the ball against the garage.

choices.text: Keep going until Mom yells dinner
choices.flavor: Thud. Thud. Thud. The neighbors stopped asking if you were okay. Mom yelled twice.

choices.text: Try to beat your own record from yesterday
choices.flavor: Yesterday was 47 catches in a row. Today is 52. Tomorrow the record falls again.

title: The Weaker Kid
description: A smaller kid wants to join your game. He is not very good. Your team is up next.

choices.text: Let them play. Put them somewhere they can help.
choices.flavor: You put them on the line. They try hard. Your team wins anyway. Good leadership.

choices.text: Tell them next game. You need to win this one.
choices.flavor: You won the game. The kid watched from the sideline. It felt different than you expected.

title: No Fear
description: A big kid is running straight at you during backyard football. Everyone else gets out of the way.

choices.text: Lower your shoulder and meet them head on
choices.flavor: BOOM. You both go down. The other kids go silent. Then someone says 'that kid is crazy.' Badge of honor.

choices.text: Stand your ground and wrap up the tackle
choices.flavor: Clean stop. Textbook. The fearless kid is also becoming a smart player.

title: New House
description: Your family is moving to a different part of town. New neighborhood, new school, new everything.

choices.text: Be excited about the fresh start
choices.flavor: New room, new kids to compete with. Change is fuel.

choices.text: Be upset about leaving friends
choices.flavor: It is hard leaving your crew. But adapting is a skill you will use forever.

title: The Loss That Stuck
description: You replayed a loss in your head for two days. Adjustments planned.

choices.text: Break down what went wrong and fix it
choices.flavor: You drew plays on notebook paper. The Xs and Os do not quite make sense yet, but the instinct is there.

choices.text: Use the anger as fuel for next time
choices.flavor: The loss burns. Good. That fire is useful.

choices.text: Shake it off and move on
choices.flavor: It is one game. There will be more. Healthy perspective at a young age.

title: Picked First
description: For the first time, you got picked first in a playground game. Both captains wanted you.

choices.text: Act like you expected it
choices.flavor: You walk over like this happens every day. It does not. But it might start.

choices.text: Pick the weaker team to prove a point
choices.flavor: Bold move. Your team is worse on paper. You carry them. Everyone remembers.

title: Choosing Harder Opponents
description: You could play with kids your age or join the older kids' game. The older kids hit harder.

choices.text: Play with the older kids
choices.flavor: You get knocked around. But you hold your own. The older kids start picking you first.

choices.text: Dominate kids your age
choices.flavor: Easy wins feel good but something is missing. You are the big fish in a small pond.

title: The Bad Day
description: You dropped an easy catch in front of everyone. They laughed. Your face is on fire.

choices.text: Go home and practice catches until your hands hurt
choices.flavor: 200 catches against the wall that evening. You will never drop that ball again.

choices.text: Laugh it off and make a joke
choices.flavor: You turn it into a bit. The laughing shifts from at you to with you. Recovery complete.

choices.text: Avoid playing for a few days
choices.flavor: The sting fades. You come back next week. But the memory lingers.

title: Captain Material
description: The game is falling apart. Kids are arguing about calls. Someone needs to take charge.

choices.text: Settle the argument and get the game moving
choices.flavor: You make the call. Both sides grumble. But they play. That is what leaders do.

choices.text: Pick sides and back your friend
choices.flavor: Loyalty is good. But picking favorites as a leader creates problems.

title: The Birthday Party
description: Your friend's birthday party is today. But the older kids said they are playing football at the park at the same time.

choices.text: Go to the park. The older kids never invite you.
choices.flavor: You showed up. You got picked last. You did not care. You were in the game. Cake acquired later.

choices.text: Go to the party. Your friend would be upset.
choices.flavor: You ate three slices of cake and won the relay race in the backyard. Good enough.

title: Faster Than Marcus
description: Marcus beat you in the race at recess. You cannot stop thinking about it. You want another shot.

choices.text: Race Marcus every day until you win
choices.flavor: Monday: lost. Tuesday: lost by less. Friday: dead tie. Next Monday: you won. Marcus wants a rematch.

choices.text: Beat Marcus at something else instead
choices.flavor: You cannot outrun him. But you can out-throw him, out-catch him, and out-tackle him. That works.

title: New Game vs. Outside
description: New video game just dropped. All your friends are playing online. But the weather is perfect.

choices.text: Go outside. The game will still be there tonight.
choices.flavor: You ran around until dark. Came home, played the game, fell asleep on the couch. Full day.

choices.text: Play the game. It is raining in your brain.
choices.flavor: You played Madden for four hours. You learned three new formations. Not a total loss.

title: Copying the Pros
description: You watched a highlight reel and now you are trying to recreate every move in the backyard.

choices.text: Practice the same juke move until you get it right
choices.flavor: Attempt 1: fell over. Attempt 15: almost. Attempt 40: clean. The grass is destroyed.

choices.text: Try every move once and keep the ones that work
choices.flavor: Spin move: no. Stiff arm: yes. Hurdle: absolutely not. Portfolio curated.

title: Playground Hierarchy
description: The fifth graders run recess. You are tired of waiting for a turn.

choices.text: Challenge the fifth graders to earn a spot
choices.flavor: You walked up and said 'I am playing.' Two kids laughed. Then you scored. Nobody laughed after that.

choices.text: Organize your own game with kids your age
choices.flavor: Your game had more players by the end of recess. The fifth graders noticed.
